# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

## Trading Phase

When posting an offer, assess whether the trade moves me closer to a complete building set rather than just improving one resource in isolation. I gave away my only ore early for grain, then later found myself unable to build because I lacked brick—the resource I'd traded away wasn't my actual bottleneck.

Before posting any offer, identify which single resource is blocking me from building, and only trade away resources I have in surplus relative to that constraint.

When I have a choice between trading partners, favor the player who has the resource I'm missing, but only if the trade is genuinely balanced. Don't assume acceptance; consider whether they benefit enough to actually say yes.

When an offer is made to me, evaluate it against my immediate building goal, not just resource diversity. A trade that feels balanced may still move me away from my target.

## Building Phase

When I cannot build because I lack one resource type, do not build a road instead—one point is not worth the wasted wood and brick when I might have no way to recover them later.

Identify my single bottleneck resource early in the game. Track which other players have it. Plan my trades multiple rounds ahead to accumulate that resource, not just react round-to-round.

In the final round especially, do not assume I'll find a trading partner for a critical resource. By round 5, if I don't have brick, I almost certainly won't get it.

## General Strategy

Do not play defensively when trailing. I ended with 3 points while p1 had 7, and I chose not to offer because I doubted success. That passivity cost me nothing but also gained me nothing. Attempt aggressive trades to catch up rather than accepting defeat early.

Settlements are worth 3 points; roads are worth 1. Direct all early trading toward settlement-building, not incremental roads.

Watch the leader's resource count and trading patterns. If one player is accumulating ore while others compete for brick, that player is likely to build settlements—I need to compete harder for the same resources or pivot to a different building strategy.

# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

**Round 1 Strategy:**
When starting with resources, calculate immediately whether you can build a settlement this round. A settlement (3 points) is vastly superior to a road (1 point), so prioritize getting the missing resource through trade rather than settling for a road. Offer your most abundant resource to secure what you need for a settlement.

**Trading Philosophy:**
When you need a specific resource to build, make targeted offers to the player who has it in abundance. Don't be shy about proposing trades early—getting a high-value build done beats hoarding resources. Accept that you may not get favorable exchange rates if it enables you to score points.

**Mid-Game Resource Management:**
After building a settlement, recognize that your resource mix will be depleted. Focus on what resources come in from yields and adjust your trading strategy accordingly. Don't assume you can keep trading the same resource away—track what you actually have round to round.

**Late-Game Building Constraints:**
When you reach rounds 4-5 with limited resources, accept that you may not be able to build again. Don't force trades trying to complete a build if you lack critical resources. Evaluate realistically whether you have all components needed (for a road: 1 wood AND 1 brick; for a settlement: 1 wood AND 1 brick AND 1 grain AND 1 ore).

**Defensive Positioning:**
When you have a commanding lead in the final round, avoid trades that give opponents resources unless you gain direct points. An offer of none is acceptable if it prevents helping competitors catch up and you cannot secure additional points yourself.

**What Did Not Work:**
I failed to rebuild momentum after round 1. My resource depletion pattern left me unable to build in rounds 4 and 5. I should have managed trades more strategically in rounds 2-3 to maintain a buildable position in later rounds, or alternatively, made more aggressive trades early to secure multiple settlements while yields were providing resources.

# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

**On Settlement vs. Road Priority**
When deciding what to build, always prioritize settlements (3 points) over roads (1 point) unless you're blocked by missing resources. The 3x point multiplier makes settlements vastly more efficient in a 5-round game. Build settlements whenever you have all four required resources.

**On Resource Trading to Enable Building**
When you identify that one resource blocks you from building a high-value structure (like needing just one brick for a settlement), actively seek trades to acquire it. Post offers that give away your abundant resources to get the missing piece. Don't hoard resources speculatively if they prevent immediate scoring.

**On Rejecting Unfavorable Trades**
When offered trades that don't move you closer to building, reject them. This includes trading away resources that are required components for your next settlement, even if the trade seems balanced. Grain and brick are particularly valuable as settlement components.

**On Late-Game Resource Abundance**
When you accumulate resources late in the game (especially ore beyond what you can build with), recognize that they may go unused. In round 4 and 5, focus on what you can actually build with what you have rather than hoping for future trades or draws.

**On Endgame Maximization**
In the final round, build any structure you have the resources for. Even a single road is better than zero points. Don't play conservatively when there are no future rounds to leverage unused resources.

**On Offensive Trading Against Leaders**
When one opponent has a significant point lead, consider whether you can trade with them to weaken their position while strengthening yours, but only if it clearly advances your own score this round. Don't sacrifice points just to hurt the leader.
